text: Salem, 1692. Witches burned at the stake.
Except... nobody was burned.
Salem: the burning myth.
It started with two girls having strange fits.
Soon, over 200 people were accused.
Courts accepted spectral evidence. Basically, dreams.
19 people were executed.
By hanging. Not fire.
In English law, witchcraft was a felony.
And felons were hanged.
Burning was more of a European thing.
One man, Giles Corey, refused to plead.
Others died in jail.
By 1693, it was over.
Later, jurors apologised.
In 2022, the last accused was finally cleared.
So where did the fire come from?
Movies and European witch trials, mixed together.
Witches burned at Salem: zero.
Anyway, here's Salem with its bonfire.
